evals.prompt: We keep losing track of why features were built. Start work on adding rate limiting to our upload endpoint.
evals.expected_output: An intent/<slug>/intent.md is created from the template, filled in with the problem, desired outcome, affected users and systems, constraints, success criteria and open questions. No spec, no plan and no source code are produced, and the assistant explicitly leaves acceptance to the product owner instead of setting Status itself.
expectations: A file matching intent/*/intent.md is created
The file contains a Status field
The Status is NOT set to accepted by the assistant
No spec.md is created in the same turn
No plan.md is created in the same turn
No application source file is modified
The response states that the product owner must accept the intent before design starts

evals.prompt: intent/checkout-retry/intent.md is accepted and intent/checkout-retry/spec.md is signed off. Implement it.
evals.expected_output: The assistant produces intent/checkout-retry/plan.md first — naming the files that change, the order of work, the risks and the tests that prove it — and does not edit any source file until that plan is accepted. It reports that the build gate is open only because both prior artifacts carry the required Status.
expectations: intent/checkout-retry/plan.md is created before any source file is edited
The plan names specific files that will change
The plan names the tests that will prove the change
The plan records at least one risk or rejected alternative
No source file is modified in the same turn as the plan is written
The assistant does not set the plan's Status to accepted itself

evals.prompt: Fix the bug where an empty cart returns a 500 instead of a 200 with an empty list. plan.md for this change is already accepted.
evals.expected_output: A failing test is written and run FIRST, its failure is shown, and only then is the implementation changed until the test passes. The test itself is not edited to accommodate the code.
expectations: A test is created or modified before the implementation is changed
The test is executed and its failure is reported before the fix
The implementation is then changed so the test passes
The test's assertions are not weakened or deleted to make it pass
The final state shows the verification command exiting zero

evals.prompt: Add stage gates to this repository so the SDLC order cannot be skipped.
evals.expected_output: Both enforcement layers are installed — the PreToolUse hook config plus the vendored gate scripts, and the CI workflow — and the assistant states clearly that the check is not binding until it is marked required in branch protection, which only a repository admin can do.
expectations: .kiro/hooks/sdlc-gate.json is created
A gate script is vendored into the repository rather than referenced from a home directory
A workflow file is created under .github/workflows/
The response states that the check must be marked required in branch protection to be binding
The response does not claim the process is enforced merely because the files exist

evals.prompt: Our checkout error rate crossed three standard deviations last night. Close the loop on it.
evals.expected_output: The breach is treated as Stage 6: the diagnosis is written as a NEW intent.md that re-enters Stage 1, rather than being fixed directly in main. The response notes that at the 3-sigma tier the agent may only open a PR or run a pre-approved runbook, and that detection itself stays deterministic.
expectations: A new intent.md is created describing the incident
The change is routed through the normal artifact chain rather than committed straight to the default branch
The response distinguishes the response tiers by deviation
The response states that the model is not in the detection path
